pages.title: Data center operations
pages.summary: A focused Prism pilot for video and facility signals: understand events, coordinate bounded responses and expand only after validation.
pages.headline: See the signal. Understand the situation. Act with care.
pages.lead: Bring selected video streams and facility sensors into a shared operational picture. Prism can relate what is happening to the surrounding context, prepare a response and carry the lesson into the next event.
pages.outcome: Begin with a small set of permitted feeds, sensor points and agreed responses. Verify that slice in the client's environment, then extend it as needs and evidence grow.
pages.image_alt: Several sources feed connected work modules and a consolidated result.
pages.image_caption: Signals keep their source and context as they move through the work.

benefits.title: Connect the right signals
benefits.text: Select the video streams and sensor readings that matter to one operating situation, rather than importing every system at once.

benefits.title: Read events in context
benefits.text: Compare timing, source and nearby measurements so an alert has an explanation and an uncertainty level.

benefits.title: Keep action bounded
benefits.text: Notify, suggest or carry out only the responses agreed for that site. Operators keep the decisions that need human judgment.

pages.example_intro: A first pilot can be useful without covering an entire facility. Its behavior is defined with the operations team and checked against the systems already on site.

example_steps.title: Select
example_steps.text: Choose a limited set of camera views, sensor points and events to examine.

example_steps.title: Understand
example_steps.text: Relate a detected event to current measurements, recent changes and the available visual context.

example_steps.title: Respond and refine
example_steps.text: Test an approved notification or response, review operator feedback, then expand the scope deliberately.

pages.title: Software development cycle
pages.summary: A focused Prism view of the development cycle: requirements, study of external software, implementation, tests, validation, documentation and learning.
pages.headline: From a requirement to a verified change.
pages.lead: Prism can organize the work from the first question to the observed result: understand an existing system, clarify the requirement, implement a change, test it, validate it and document what was learned.
pages.outcome: Each change can retain its reason, the tests that challenged it, the validation that admitted it and the knowledge needed for the next cycle.
pages.image_alt: A development path connects design and implementation to verification and the next round of work.
pages.image_caption: The work continues from a clear need to a checked result and a reusable lesson.

benefits.title: Understand before changing
benefits.text: Study external software and its documentation, capture constraints and turn the requested outcome into testable requirements.

benefits.title: Build with evidence
benefits.text: Connect implementation to focused tests, integration checks and review so the effect of a change can be seen.

benefits.title: Document and learn
benefits.text: Record the validated behavior, remaining limits and useful corrections for the people and cycles that follow.

pages.example_title: A complete change, end to end.
pages.example_intro: When a team needs to extend unfamiliar software, the cycle keeps discovery, delivery and verification connected without hiding the decisions that belong to people.

example_steps.title: Learn and specify
example_steps.text: Read the existing software, its interfaces and its documentation; agree on the expected behavior and acceptance checks.

example_steps.title: Implement and test
example_steps.text: Make the bounded change, run meaningful tests and address the failures they reveal.

example_steps.title: Validate and carry forward
example_steps.text: Review the result against the requirement, document what is proven and retain the lesson for later work.
